sam_support: Customer 'LambdaHealth' pasted this: repeated 429 responses starting ~2025-11-09T09:02:00Z, most incidents hit within the first 10s of the minute. They say their client is multiplexing streams and they see an RPM/TPM breach. Logs below.

sam_support: ```
2025-11-09T09:01:59.912Z INFO request id=req_abc user=lambdahealth endpoint=/v1/generate tokens=1845
2025-11-09T09:02:00.031Z WARN rate_limiter reject id=req_def user=lambdahealth reason=tpms_exceeded
2025-11-09T09:02:02.210Z WARN rate_limiter reject id=req_ghi user=lambdahealth reason=tpms_exceeded
2025-11-09T09:02:05.411Z WARN rate_limiter reject id=req_jkl user=lambdahealth reason=requests_per_minute
```

marta: Are we confident this is token-window (TPM) and not just short-request bursts hitting RPM? Customer mentions lots of streaming chunks which could inflate tokens.

chris_sre: From infra metrics I see a sharp token consumption spike at 09:02:00 UTC aligned to minute boundary. Aggregator shows token_window[user=lambdahealth][09:02] = 55k, limit=30k. requests_window spikes smaller (~2.4k) while limit=5k. So TPM is dominant.

sam_support: Nice — customer also said they disable streaming for some call paths but still see issues. Could be multiple clients hitting same API key with different code paths.

eng_runtime_oncall: Quick triage ideas: 1) confirm whether top-of-minute bursting is due to many small streams committing tokens at final flush; 2) check if our token bucket uses a minute-aligned window vs rolling window; minute-aligned can create boundary clumping. I'll pull rate_limiter config.

deploybot: Deploy #r-limiter-2025-11-07 is active on prod-edge-2 (commit 7a9f2b3). Rate limiter policy: fixed_minute_window=true, per_customer=true, smoothing_disabled=false.

marta: If it's fixed_minute_window that's probably the issue — bursts from many clients that only flush tokens at end of stream will all land in the same minute. Recommend switching to rolling window or enabling inter-minute smoothing for this customer.

chris_sre: Short-term mitigation we can suggest to customer: add client-side jitter on flush, stagger background jobs to avoid top-of-minute alignment, reduce per-connection concurrency, and implement exponential backoff with Retry-After parsing. We should also set a temporary quota bump if needed.

sam_support: I told customer to implement jitter and reduce concurrent streams; they asked for a concrete repro we can run on our side. They provided a small curl loop that simulates multiple streaming connections.

sam_support: ```
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" \n    -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{"prompt":"x...","max_tokens":1024}' &
done
wait
```

eng_runtime_oncall: Can reproduce locally against staging. With fixed_minute_window we see token spikes at minute boundaries and rejections. With rolling window smoothing_enabled=true rejections drop ~85%.

marta: Action plan: 1) Support - advise customer to add jitter + backoff (complete), and offer temporary TPM increase (pending). 2) Eng_runtime - evaluate turning on rolling window or smoothing for per-customer policies; if safe, enable gradual rollout for customers with streaming workloads. 3) SRE - monitor other customers for similar minute-boundary patterns.

chris_sre: I've created internal issue: INF-2025-834 - "minute-window -> rolling-window policy for streaming-heavy keys" and linked customer's case. Added alert: token_spikes_minute_boundary > 3 customers -> pager.

sam_support: Customer accepted jitter test plan and asked for a temporary +50% TPM while they roll out client changes. I started a quota request.

deploybot: Quota change request Q-59213 opened for lambdahealth, requested +50% TPM, pending billing approval.

eng_runtime_oncall: I'll prototype an opt-in smoothing flag for Dedicated/Hosted in staging; if low-risk we can flip for affected keys only.

marta: TL;DR for support reply to customer: TPM is the root cause due to minute-aligned token flushes. Short-term: add jitter, reduce concurrency, use exponential backoff, or request a temporary TPM increase. Long-term: we'll offer rolling-window smoothing to prevent minute-boundary clumping. :thumbsup: 

chris_sre: marking this thread for follow-up after quota decision and eng runtime experiment.

sam_support: Thanks all — closing loop with customer now and will paste their confirmation when they respond. :white_check_mark:
